Incumbent Senator [[Richard Shelby]] was [[1986 United States Senate election in Alabama|first elected in 1986]] and [[1992 United States Senate election in Alabama|re-elected in 1992]] as a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] before becoming a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] in [[Republican Revolution|1994]].{{cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/the-last-time-alabama-elected-a-democrat-to-the-senate-richard-shelby-2017-12?r=US&IR=T|title=The last Democrat to win an Alabama Senate race later became a Republican -- and did not vote for Roy Moore|website=Business Insider|last1=Chan|first1=Tara Francis|date=December 13, 2017|access-date=August 7, 2020}} In February 2021, Shelby announced that he would not seek re-election to a seventh term, which resulted in the first open Senate seat since [[1996 United States Senate election in Alabama|1996]] and the first in this seat since [[1968 United States Senate election in Alabama|1968]].{{efn|[[Maryon Pittman Allen]] ran for this Class III seat in the [[1978 United States Senate special election in Alabama|special election in 1978]] following the death of her husband [[James Allen (Alabama politician)|James Allen]], but lost in the Democratic primary to [[Donald Stewart (Alabama politician)|Donald Stewart]], who won the election. Stewart ran for re-election to a full term in [[1980 United States Senate election in Alabama|1980]], but lost in the Democratic primary to [[Jim Folsom Jr.|Jim Folsom]].}} Primary elections in Alabama were held on May 24, with Will Boyd securing the Democratic nomination. However, as none of the Republican candidates received at least 50% of the vote, a runoff election occurred on June 21 between the top two candidates of the first round: attorney [[Katie Britt]] and U.S. representative [[Mo Brooks]]. Britt won the runoff against Brooks and subsequently became the Republican nominee.{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-politics-alabama-presidential-donald-trump-9cabff79c0ab2d2611c55059962f5100|title=Britt wins tumultuous Alabama Senate race scrambled by Trump|last1=Colvin|first1=Jill|last2=Chandler|first2=Kim|work=Associated Press|date=June 21, 2022|accessdate=June 21, 2022}} Britt's victory in the Republican Party primary was seen as [[tantamount to election]] in Alabama, which is a heavily Republican state.{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/news/2022/06/katie-britt-on-her-way-to-becoming-the-first-woman-to-be-elected-senator-in-alabama.html|title=Katie Britt wins runoff, stands to become first woman elected senator in Alabama|last=Whites-Koditschek|first=Sarah|work=AL.com|date=June 21, 2022|accessdate=June 21, 2022}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/21/us/politics/katie-britt-mo-brooks.html|title=Katie Britt leveraged her Alabama connections and political savvy to trounce Mo Brooks|last1=Ulloa|first1=Jazmine|last2=Hounshell|first2=Blake|work=The New York Times|date=June 21, 2022|accessdate=June 21, 2022}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2022/06/21/1106484159/alabama-republican-senate-runoff-results-brooks-britt|title=Trump-backed Britt defeats Brooks in Alabama Republican Senate runoff|last=Bustillo|first=Ximena|work=National Public Radio|date=June 21, 2022|accessdate=June 21, 2022}} Britt won the general election and became the first [[Women in the United States Senate|woman]] elected to the U.S. Senate in the state's history.{{efn|Alabama had never elected a female senator in the state's history. Two previous female senators, [[Dixie Bibb Graves|Dixie Graves]] and Maryon Pittman Allen, were appointed to the Senate, but were never nominated in a Senate election.}} ==Republican primary== Early polling showed U.S. Representative [[Mo Brooks]] as the frontrunner in the race, and he received the endorsement of former president [[Donald Trump]].{{cite web | url=https://headtopics.com/us/brooks-trump-adviser-to-make-campaign-announcement-19320253 | title=Brooks, Trump adviser to make campaign announcement | date=March 22, 2021 }} However, in November, the race started becoming increasingly closer with former chief of staff to incumbent senator [[Richard Shelby]], [[Katie Britt]], running neck and neck with Brooks. In March 2022, businessman and former pilot [[Michael Durant]] took the lead in the race, with Brooks only just beginning to spend money on television advertisements. On March 23, 2022, with Brooks polling in third place, Trump revoked his endorsement and promised to endorse a new candidate.{{cite web | url=https://www.npr.org/2022/03/23/1088264503/donald-trump-mo-brooks-withdraws-alabama-endorsement | title=Trump yanks endorsement of Alabama Senate candidate Brooks, who said to get past 2020 | website=NPR | date=March 23, 2022 | last1=Gonyea | first1=Don }} In his official statement, Trump slammed Brooks for wanting to move past the [[2020 United States presidential election]], and claimed he went "woke" on it. There was speculation that Trump withdrew his endorsement because he did not want to be associated with a losing campaign. Brooks claimed that Trump had told him to reinstate him as president and that Trump had been manipulated by Senate Minority Leader [[Mitch McConnell]]. Brooks attacked Britt as allegedly being weak on illegal immigration and supporting higher taxes, while Brooks' critics frequently point to his long career in politics, having been in office for 40 years.{{cite web | url=https://www.waff.com/2022/03/23/rep-mo-brooks-responds-trumps-latest-comments/ | title=Rep.
